messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw a cluster of SLO breaches on embeds yesterday around 03:12 UTC. Looks correlated with mixed-dim bulk ingest that ends up routed to slowpath. Our telemetry sampling was too sparse to pinpoint. Can we decide on a better sampling + bucketing scheme?
liam: +1. Proposal: deterministic dim bucketing + reservoir sampling per (tenant_tier, model, dim_bucket). Sample ~0.5-1% of steady traffic but ALWAYS keep traces for oversize batches. Buckets: 1-64, 65-256, 257+. Limit ~10k samples/min total.
anya: Cardinality concern — tenant+model+bucket+route will blow up metrics. If we do reservoir per-tenant we can OOM. Instead map tenant -> tier (free/prod/enterprise) and sample per-tier+bucket. For deeper digs we can use `tenant_hash_mod_100` as a debug key.
david: Agree on buckets. Also capture minimal fields: model, dim, batch_size, route_decision, split_count, latency_ms. Keep vector payload out. Example telemetry JSON: `{"model":"text-embed-xxl","dim":1536,"batch_size":120,"route":"fastpath","split_count":1,"latency_ms":42}`
liam: For metrics ingestion we should emit low-cardinality aggregates only, e.g. `embedding.requests_total{dim_range="65-256",route="fastpath"}` and histograms for latency by dim_range. Avoid tenant id in prometheus labels.
maya: @anya +1 on tenant tiering. Also recommend deterministic hash sampling so a tenant is either in or out of sampling window for consistency.
anya: Sticky sampling is important — flipping sample decisions randomly across minutes makes reproducing failures nearly impossible. Deterministic (hash % N) sampling per tenant works.
david: Rollout plan: gate behind feature flag `embed_telemetry_v2`. Canary 5% tenants for 24h, then 25%, then all. Keep oversize traces never-sampled (always-on) to get ground truth.
console-bot: Dashboard ask: add "Embeddings SLO by dim_range" tile + heatmap for split_count vs p95 latency. Also show current `sample_rate` for each tenant tier and provide a support toggle to increase sampling for a specific tenant_id.
maya: Ops Q — how expensive is storing the trace payload? We should only persist meta and maybe first 64 bytes of raw input. No full vectors.
liam: Storage plan: compress traces, TTL 7d, redact raw inputs unless tenant explicitly opts into debug retention (PII rules). Keep trace size under ~2KB typical.
anya: Telemetry schema must be versioned. Existing v1 was raw dims+latency. v2 adds `dim_bucket`, `route_decision`, `tenant_tier`, `split_count`. Update docs and SDKs.
david: I'll open the proto + console mock PRs. @maya can you own the canary tenant list (prod vs non-prod mix) for the 5%?
maya: On it — assembling CSV of candidate tenants now, will DM the list and paste in here. :thumbsup:
ingress-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: `embed-telemetry-v2` -> canary-5pct at 2024-04-02T06:00:00Z (automated).
liam: Quick query for dashboards (prometheus-ish): `sum(rate(embedding_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (dim_range)` — that plus `split_count` breakdown should surface regressions quickly.
anya: One more: add an explainability field `routing_reason` (e.g., "kv_cache_miss", "oversize_split") but keep it coarse to avoid label explosion.
maya: Decision summary: dim buckets (1-64,65-256,257+), deterministic tenant-tier sampling, always-on oversized traces, telemetry v2 proto + canary 5% -> 24h -> wider. Action owners: david=proto+PR, maya=canary list, liam=metrics plumbing, anya=cardinality guardrails.
liam: Sounds good. I'll prep the reservoir sampler lib and a small change to the ingest path to attach `tenant_tier`.
maya: Thanks all — will follow up once CSV is ready."
